summary: ValenceBio: Maintenance-triggered control-plane failover caused heartbeat storm, streaming silence and duplicate completions — customer escalation & post-incident action plan
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled maintenance window for a private control plane (TLS/HSM rotation) on 2026-03-05 02:10 UTC, ValenceBio began experiencing sustained streaming silence for conversational endpoints followed by a burst of duplicate completions and elevated token billing over a ~45 minute window. Customer escalated to Support (phone) at 02:30 UTC reporting timeouts and mismatched transcripts.

Impact:
- In-session streaming responses stopped for approximately 8-30s per session before abrupt connection resets.
- When streams resumed some requests produced duplicate completions (2x identical final chunks) causing inflated token usage and billing exposure.
- A subset of long-running conversations saw partial transcript loss requiring client retries.
- Estimated customer-visible error rate peaked at ~12% for impacted endpoints.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) using Redwood Private control plane with HSM-backed key rotation.
- Region: prod-us-east.
- Models: redwood-v2-medium (primary) with redwood-v1-quantized fallback.

Timeline (high level):
- 02:05 UTC: Scheduled control-plane maintenance begins (TLS cert + HSM rotation).
- 02:10 UTC: Automated control-plane failover triggered to secondary cluster.
- 02:12-02:40 UTC: Observability shows repeated TLS renegotiation attempts and a large increase in keepalive/heartbeat traffic between private agents and control plane.
- 02:20 UTC: First customer phone escalation.
- 02:28 UTC: Streaming silence and reconnects observed from ValenceBio production instances.
- 02:45 UTC: Mitigation applied: throttle heartbeat retry policy and force-stable control-plane endpoint for ValenceBio.
- 03:00 UTC: Duplicate completion pattern subsides; customer confirms partial restoration.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1. Simulate control-plane certificate rotation against private agent group with aggressive keepalive backoff configured.
2. Observe repeated TLS session renegotiation and broker re-registration loops on agent side under peak load.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Temporarily disabled aggressive keepalive fast-retry on private agents for ValenceBio pool.
- Forced agents onto stable control-plane endpoint to prevent oscillating reconnection.
- Applied temporary routing rule to pin ValenceBio to a single compatible model variant to reduce fallback-induced duplicate completions.

Why this is customer-impacting and unique:
- Private deployments with HSM/TLS rotations require exact sequencing; our current agent backoff and re-registration code did not gracefully handle transient control-plane unavailability and re-auth flows, resulting in heartbeat storms that overwhelmed the serving-runtime broker and caused partial duplicate message delivery.

Communication status:
- Customer notified in incident call at 02:35 UTC.
- Formal incident update e-mail sent at 04:20 UTC with timeline and initial remediation.

Next steps and post-incident actions (high level):
- Engineering to patch agent re-registration logic to add jitter and exponential backoff for TLS renegotiation (INT-78321).
- Add canary sequence for HSM rotations that verifies control-plane stable handoff before wide rotation (INT-78322).
- Billing: review ValenceBio token usage between 02:05-03:00 UTC for retroactive crediting.
- Customer follow-up meeting scheduled for 2026-03-09 to review RCA and credits.

investigation_notes: Broker logs 2026-03-05T02:12-02:40 UTC show repeated REGISTER/UNREGISTER cycles from the same agent IDs correlating with TLS handshake errors (openssl_code: CERT_VERIFY_FAILED) until rotation completed.
Serving runtime metrics: spike in orphaned stream completions and duplicate final chunk emissions correlated with agent reconnect bursts.
Control-plane audit shows HSM key rotation steps completed but secondary did not signal stable state to agent discovery API due to a transient DB schema lock on rotation transaction.

Telemetry indicates fallback to redwood-v1-quantized occurred during reconnects; duplicate completion behavior appears when both primary and fallback emit finalization events during a reconnection window.
No evidence of data corruption; transcripts either truncated or duplicated, consistent with session reattachment semantics rather than model inference error.
resolution_notes: Hotfix deployed to private-agent (v1.14.1) to add randomized exponential backoff for TLS re-registration and to suppress double-finalization during rapid reconnects.
Control-plane runbook updated: HSM rotation now performs a 'stable handoff' check via discovery API before advertising new endpoint to agents.
Routing rule temporarily pinned ValenceBio to redwood-v2-medium during remediation window to avoid fallback amplification; unpinned after verification.
Billing team initiated usage audit and is preparing a customer credit proposal for the window 02:05-03:00 UTC. (Finance ticket FIN-4821)
Customer-facing postmortem published to Confluence and shared with ValenceBio; follow-up meeting completed on 2026-03-09.
follow_up_tasks: INT-78321 - Add jittered exponential backoff and connection state guards to private-agent re-registration logic.
INT-78322 - Implement canary gating for HSM/TLS rotations with automated discovery health checks.
INT-78323 - Add metric and alert for duplicate completion rate > 0.5% for any customer over 5m window.
INT-78324 - Billing reconciliation: compute retroactive credit for ValenceBio and issue invoice adjustment (owner: Finance).
